definitions.explanation: A grand, far-reaching goal for one's life — bigger than ordinary career or personal goals. A formal, somewhat literary word, famous from William S. Clark's saying {少年|しょうねん}よ、{大志|たいし}を{抱|いだ}け ("Boys, be ambitious").

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いうちに{大志|たいし}を{持|も}つことが{大切|たいせつ}だ。
examples.english: It's important to have great ambitions while young.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{大志|たいし}を{抱|いだ}いて{故郷|こきょう}を{離|はな}れ、{都会|とかい}へ{向|む}かった。
examples.english: Holding lofty ambitions, he left his hometown and headed for the city.

notes:
Compound of {大|たい} (great) + {志|し} (will, intention). A formal noun, often paired with {抱|いだ}く (to hold, to harbor).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {大志|たいし}を{抱|いだ}く: to harbor great ambitions
- {大志|たいし}を{持|も}つ: to have great ambitions
- {少年|しょうねん}よ、{大志|たいし}を{抱|いだ}け: "Boys, be ambitious" (famous Clark quote)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {志|こころざし}: aspiration; will — broader, also formal
- {野望|やぼう}: ambition — often with a negative ring of selfish or excessive desire
- {野心|やしん}: ambition; aspiration — can be neutral or negative depending on context
- {夢|ゆめ}: dream — everyday word, less formal
